# Leveraging Visualizations and MLflow for In-depth Model Analysis

## Introduction

In any machine learning project, understanding the behavior, performance, and characteristics of the
developed models is important. Clear, informative visualizations play a crucial role in this understanding,
offering insights into the model's patterns, errors, and efficiency.

In this portion of the guide, we look at a notebook that is concerned with the generation and storage of
common and useful plots associated with a regression task.

We'll be looking at two primary means of logging plots along with our logged models:

- **Direct plot logging** via `mlflow.log_figure()` we will use an in-memory figure reference to a generated plot.
- **Logging a local plot file** via `mlflow.log_artifact()` to allow us to log a locally stored image to the run.

## Role of Visualizations in Model Analysis

Visualizations act as a window into the intricate world of machine learning models. They enable the exploration of various aspects:

- **Understanding Data**: Initial visualizations allow for a deep dive into the data, revealing patterns, anomalies, and relationships that can inform the entire modeling process.
- **Model Evaluation**: Plots such as residual plots and prediction error plots help in diagnosing issues with the model and evaluating its performance.
- **Hyperparameter Tuning**: Visualization aids in understanding the impact of different hyperparameters on the model's performance, guiding the selection process.
- **Error Analysis**: They help in analyzing the types and patterns of errors made by the model, providing insight into possible improvements.

### A Warning about Procedural Generation of Plots

In the accompanying notebook to this subsection of this guide, you will observe plots being declared
within functions. This approach deviates from the typical examples seen in machine learning tutorials
and guides, so it's essential to clarify why this method is chosen for the provided examples.

**The Central Issue: Statefulness**

rows.title: Add `mlflow.genai.compare_evaluations` for paired statistical comparison of evaluation runs
rows.excerpt:
<!--
Do not remove any sections. Remove unused checkboxes except for the patch release section at the bottom.
Use backticks for code references and file paths in the PR title (e.g., `ClassName`, `function_name`, `utils.py`).
-->

### Related Issues/PRs

<!-- 🚨 Choose either "Closes" (auto-close on merge) or "Relates to" (reference only). 🚨 -->

Closes #26193

### What changes are proposed in this pull request?

<!-- Please fill in changes proposed in this PR. -->

Adds an experimental `mlflow.genai.compare_evaluations(candidate_run_id, baseline_run_id, ...)`: a paired, per-scorer statistical comparison of two GenAI evaluation runs. Client-side only (scipy, no server or store changes), as agreed on #26193.

**Pairing:** rows are paired on the eval request id when both runs evaluated the same static dataset; otherwise (e.g. runs that used `predict_fn`, where `evaluate()` assigns fresh ids per run) on a stable hash of the inputs. This corrects a claim in the issue: pairing on the id is only free for static datasets, and the docs say so. Unpaired rows, including duplicate keys within a run, are reported rather than matched by position; fewer than two pairs gives `insufficient_pairs` for that scorer.

**Statistics per scorer:** difference (candidate − baseline); binary values → McNemar (exact below 25 discordant pairs, chi-square with continuity correction above); numeric → Wilcoxon signed-rank by default, with paired t reported alongside; percentile bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples, fixed seed) at `confidence_level` (default 0.95); Cohen's d_z; ties counted. Zero-variance deltas are handled explicitly: all-zero → p = 1; constant non-zero → paired t and effect size are undefined and reported as NaN, while Wilcoxon is still computed and used.

**Direction:** GenAI scorers carry no `greater_is_better`, so scorers default to higher-is-better with a per-scorer override (`greater_is_better={"latency": False}`). This only affects `assert_improved`; `diff` is always candidate − baseline.

**Results:** returns a `ComparisonResult` with `summary()` (DataFrame) and `assert_improved(scorers, alpha)` for CI gating. With `log_results=True` (default), it logs `compare/<baseline_short_id>/<scorer>/{diff,ci_low,ci_high,p_value,effect_size,n_paired}` metrics on the candidate run (short id = first 8 characters, so several baselines don't overwrite each other)

rows.title: Attach cited media to triage reports
rows.excerpt:
### Related Issues/PRs

Context: [PR #26352](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/26352) introduced the triage skill. Prior text-only dry runs passed at [run 37453638855](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/37453638855) and [run 37453642718](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/37453642718); neither exercised media.

### What changes are proposed in this pull request?

Triage could capture UI evidence under `/tmp/triage-out/media`, but the workflow uploaded only `payload.json`, leaving cited local paths broken. This carries media to `post_triage` and uses the existing `skills embed-media` command to upload cited files and rewrite their references on live runs.

- Update triage and bug instructions to save useful captures under `$out_dir/media`, cite exact absolute paths, and validate citations.
- Preserve media paths in the payload artifact; validate before previewing, then rewrite and revalidate the comment before posting.
- Keep dry runs mutation- and upload-free; show validated local references as unpublished.
- Scope `UPLOAD_MEDIA_TOKEN` to the live upload step. Uncited captures remain unattached; failed uploads degrade to readable prose.

```bash
jq -j .comment "$out_dir/payload.json" |
  uv run --directory .claude/skills --package skills skills embed-media \
    --check --dir "$out_dir/media"
```

### How is this PR tested?

- [ ] Existing unit/integration tests
- [ ] New unit/integration tests
- [x] Manual tests

Manual workflow checks on [issue #25718](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/25718):

- [Opus dry run](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/37458618977): validated two screenshot references with no warnings; did not post or upload media.
- [Live Opus run](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/37462365338): validated and uploaded one cited screenshot, embedded its GitHub attachment URL in the [posted triage comment](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/25718#issuecomment-6016101912), and applied `triage: already-fixed`.

The live run could not capture the 3.16.0 view because that UI stayed on its loading skeleton in the sandbox. It still verified the live media upload and comment posting path with the current-checkout screenshot. No local tests were run.
